To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
deep ReLU networks see a manifold structure on the data and this structure is model-centric, i.e., it depends on the model.
the model sees the data through the lens of the data leaf, a low-dimensional Rieamnnian manifold, and that the data leaf is a subset of the data manifold.
the data manifold is a model-centric manifold and that the model-centric manifold has a data leaf of dimension bounded by the number of classification labels.

the question: how does the model see the data?

deep neural networks are able to learn a low-dimensional manifold on which the data lie, and the dimension is related to the number of classes.

deep ReLU classifiers see the data through a manifold structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data manifold is a model-centric manifold, and the data leaf is a model-centric data leaf.
a deep ReLU neural net classifier sees a data leaf as an Riemannian submanifold, and it can learn a classification function on the data leaf, which is a function on a Riemannian manifold.
the data manifold is model-centric, as it is seen through the model parameters.

the model can see the structure of the data, and this is a first step towards understanding the role of deep learning models in data representation.
a deep neural network can learn the geometry of the data, and that this geometry is a function of the data variables only.
